OLD_PIPELINE_INFORMATION_LOSS: PARTIAL (finite_int64 int-truncation drops the fractional part of get_volume output; the mapping raw -> int(get_volume(raw)) is not injective, so raw cannot be recovered from canonical)
INVERTIBILITY_NOTE: canonical = int(old_get_volume(raw))*100. The pre-image of a canonical value is a finite set of raws; for values >= 256 both a normal-band raw (IEEE==old_int) and an anomalous-band raw (IEEE!=old_int) exist, so the raw is not uniquely recoverable from the retained value alone. Amount VWAP cross-validation disambiguates most rows.

CLASSIFIER.normal_band: lp>=0x43 (>=256 lots): int(OLD)==int(NEW) for all raw; dense in integers >= 256, so any value >= 256 absent from the divergence table is PROVABLY_UNAFFECTED
CLASSIFIER.divergence_band: lp 0x3c..0x42 full 24-bit mantissa preimage table (old_int -> set(int(NEW)))
CLASSIFIER.row_validation: amount VWAP (amount / volume) inside [low, high]: if OLD VWAP is already plausible the row is treated unaffected (economically self-consistent); PROVABLY_AFFECTED only when OLD VWAP outside range AND corrected VWAP inside range
CLASSIFIER.UNKNOWN_NOTE: AMBIGUOUS is never demoted to unaffected
